note: The eleven node types and how the directory groups each one. Order here is the order on the front page.

entries.name: Amulets
entries.blurb: The things themselves: worn, buried, nailed above a door, folded into a pocket.

entries.name: Traditions
entries.blurb: The whole practice a charm belongs to, and who is entitled to make one.

entries.name: Signs
entries.blurb: An eye, a hand, a horn, a knot, a serpent — the marks that travel between traditions.

entries.name: Materials
entries.blurb: Carnelian, iron, amber, coral, paper, hair, salt. What a charm is cut from is half of what it claims.

entries.name: Practices
entries.blurb: Making, charging, wearing, feeding, retiring. A charm is a verb before it is a noun.

entries.name: Places
entries.blurb: Markets, workshops, shrines, dig sites and the museum rooms where the rest of it ended up.

entries.name: People
entries.blurb: Makers, monks, excavators, collectors, the scholars who wrote the catalogues.

entries.name: Museums and projects
entries.blurb: Who holds the objects, who publishes the images, who is asking for them back.

entries.name: Words
entries.blurb: Amulet, talisman, charm, ta'wiz, omamori, nazar — and what each one actually says.

entries.name: Pictures
entries.blurb: Catalogue plates, shop signs, votive walls, the drawn sign itself.

entries.name: Long reads
entries.blurb: The eye across four continents, the fake market, and who a charm in a case belongs to.
